content.text: {"primary_meaning":"God’s righteous evaluation of human persons, deeds, peoples, or powers, resulting in a just verdict—vindication or condemnation—and often in reward, punishment, or separation. In Christian teaching, “judgment” most commonly points especially to the final, eschatological judgment by God through Christ.","primary_basis":["Ecclesiastes 12:14 — God brings every deed, including hidden things, into judgment.","Matthew 25:31–46 — the Son of Man separates the righteous from the wicked and assigns their respective destinies.","John 5:22–29 — the Father entrusts judgment to the Son, followed by resurrection to life or judgment.","Acts 17:31 — God has appointed a day to judge the world in righteousness through the risen Christ.","Romans 2:5–16 — God’s impartial judgment assesses deeds and hidden things.","2 Corinthians 5:10 — all appear before Christ’s judgment seat to receive according to what they have done.","Revelation 20:11–15 — the dead are judged before the great white throne according to their deeds."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Historical or temporal divine judgment: God acts within history against individuals, nations, cities, or oppressive powers through disaster, defeat, exile, or societal collapse.","basis":["Genesis 6–9","Exodus 7–12","2 Kings 17:5–23","2 Kings 25:1–21","Isaiah 13:1–22","Jeremiah 25:8–14","Revelation 18:1–24"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Condemnation or punitive sentence specifically, rather than the whole neutral process of evaluation. In many passages “judgment” functions almost synonymously with adverse verdict, wrath, or destruction.","basis":["John 3:18–19","John 12:31","Romans 5:16–18","2 Peter 2:4–9","Jude 6–15"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Disciplinary, corrective, or purifying judgment directed toward God’s people, intended to expose sin, produce repentance, or restore holiness rather than merely condemn.","basis":["1 Corinthians 11:29–32","Hebrews 12:5–11","1 Peter 4:17","Revelation 3:19"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Vindication and deliverance: judgment is good news for the oppressed because God condemns evil, establishes justice, and publicly vindicates the faithful.","basis":["Psalm 9:7–10","Psalm 96:10–13","Isaiah 11:1–5","Luke 18:7–8","Revelation 6:9–11","Revelation 19:1–2"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Moral discernment or self-examination by believers, including distinguishing right from wrong and assessing oneself before God.","basis":["1 Corinthians 6:1–5","1 Corinthians 11:28–31","1 Corinthians 14:29","Hebrews 5:14"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus on the core meaning of divine evaluation and just verdict, especially in relation to final judgment. However, “judgment” is not a symbol with one rigid referent in every passage: context determines whether it emphasizes evaluation, condemnation, temporal punishment, discipline, separation, or vindication."}
